newsitem.title: UK: Brent cash market weaker, but wet barrels bid up.
newsitem.headline: Brent cash market weaker, but wet barrels bid up.

text.p: The North Sea Brent cash market eased lower on Tuesday, but remaining April wet barrels were bid slightly higher, traders said.
The May/June Brent intermonth spread was actively traded ahead of the expiry of the May IPE contract at the close of business.

May/June sold in Singapore at a low of -30 cents, before trading at -25 cents and -27 cents in London, more than five cents down on Monday. On the IPE, the May/June spread eased back by 14 cents to trade at -29 cents at 1234 GMT, having settled above paper market levels on Monday.
The IPE May Brent contract was 30 cents down at $17.89 a barrel, after a full paper cargo traded at $18.08.
But CFDs were only slightly weaker with next week's dates (April 21-25) actively traded between June Brent -60 cents and -63 cents, and remaining April wet cargoes were bid firmer.

At least two trading houses bid May Brent -50 cents, five cents up from Monday's deal. Offers were also firmer with one seller looking for next week's CFD levels "plus a few cents", roughly the equivalent of May Brent -35/-30 cents.
Traders said that transatlantic sales wee helping to clear out the overhang of April barrels.
A European major last week sold two cargoes into the Louisiana Offshore Oil Port (LOOP) at around June WTI -$1.00. The Brents were destined for Canada and more were on offer this week, traders said.

The May Brent programme released on Tuesday scheduled the equivalent of 41.8 cargoes, or two full 500,000 barrel cargoes more than the revised April programme. Traders said the higher programme was due to the longer month and a slightly lighter maintenance schedule on the Brent system than in April.
"We expected it to be a bit higher anyway so it's not too dramatic," said one.
West African barrels proved difficult to move with no interest in the Mediterranean and only limited buying from the U.S., sellers said.
Forcados was offered at last done level of dated Brent -25 cents with buyers five cents lower.

Qua Iboe was under pressure with ample supplies unsold in April, including a VLCC in the last decade. Buying for India has cleared out much of the first decade May but second decade onwards was heavily loaded. The grade was assessed around dated Brent +5/+10 cents.
Bonny Light was holding around dated Brent +15 cents.
But lack of buying interest on Bonny Medium saw some traders pegging this grade as low as dated Brent -40 cents.

Berth number one at Novorossisk was closed early on Tuesday due to high southerly winds and swell. Shipping sources expected the port to close fully for the day once the vessel loading at berth two has completed.
